reduceIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE below $78,536.1 AND a failure to reclaim it on either of the next two hourly bars. That is the low of the 14:00Z reclaim bar - the exact bar that turned the flush - so losing it on a settled close means the reclaim itself has failed rather than merely been retested. Spot is 604.6 points above it, which is 0.89 hourly ATRs at the current 682.75. The two-bar reclaim clause is retained and it has now earned its keep twice in one day: morning's gate at 78,880.0 was breached on a settled close and then reclaimed on the very next bar, which is precisely the wick-not-confirmation failure the clause exists to filter.

addIf.confirmation: A settled 1H CLOSE above $79,571.4 - the session high since morning, printed on the 16:00Z bar and immediately rejected back to 79,070. Spot is 430.7 points below it. Closing above that rejection high would confirm the reclaim is extending rather than stalling, and would put the 79,999.8 handle back in play as the next objective.

operations.note: Still flat and still the right call, though for a different reason than at morning. Morning stayed out because direction was two-sided; midday stays out because price is sitting almost exactly in the middle of a 1,443.8 point session range with the heaviest and most evenly-contested liquidation bucket on the board 109 points overhead. A long needs its stop under 78,536.1, which is 605 points of risk for a first objective 431 points away - that is negative expectancy before anything else is considered. A short is worse: it would be selling 1,013 points off the low into a market where the long side has already been liquidated 5.34-to-1 and open interest is still falling. Leverage gets deployed at the edges of this range, not from the middle of it.

calibration.rollingRecord: Across the last nine graded sessions the desk is 2 marginal wins, 5 losses and 2 near-flat. Today's result adds a genuinely new finding rather than restating the old one. The corrected lesson midnight and morning arrived at was 'this desk enters at the EXTREME of a move in whichever direction it happens to be leaning'. Morning's trim is a third data point for it: it sold at 79,161.2 into the worst momentum reading of the day, and price is 79,140.7 six hours later after touching 78,127.6 and 79,571.4 in between. But the more useful observation is about the GATE rather than the trade. Morning wrote a two-bar reclaim clause into its reduce level, the level was breached on a settled close, the reclaim happened on the very next bar, and the clause correctly stopped the desk from selling 1,013 points off the low. That clause has now saved a bad exit once and, in the same day, failed to save one when it was omitted from the invalidation level. The finding: gates written with a reclaim clause have outperformed bare price levels, and the invalidation should carry one too.
